questions.enonce_markdown: "Economic goods are scarce goods". The meaning of the word "scarce" in this quotation is that
questions.corrige_markdown: In economics, scarcity does not mean that a good is rare in absolute terms. It means that resources, and therefore the goods they produce, are limited in supply relative to the unlimited wants of people, so choices must be made and an opportunity cost is incurred. Option D states exactly this relationship between limited goods and unlimited wants. A is wrong because a good can be abundant in quantity and still be scarce (for example rice or cement). B refers to effective demand (wants backed by money), which is not the definition. C talks about households only and not about wants. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: there are very few of these goods.
there are insufficient goods to meet effective demand at a given time.
the goods are limited in supply to households.
there are not enough of the goods to meet all our wants.

questions.enonce_markdown: The aspect of economics which is concerned with answering the question of 'what is?' or 'what will be?' is
questions.corrige_markdown: Positive economics deals with objective statements about facts and cause and effect, which can in principle be tested against evidence: 'what is' and 'what will be' (for example, a rise in the price of cocoa will reduce the quantity demanded). Normative economics deals with value judgements, 'what ought to be' (for example, the government should reduce income inequality). Deductive and inductive are methods of reasoning, not branches of economics defined by the question asked. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a mixed economy,
questions.corrige_markdown: A mixed economy combines a private sector, where the price mechanism allocates resources, with a public sector run by the state. Because the market still operates for a large part of output, consumers keep some power to direct production through their spending: there is some degree of consumer sovereignty. A describes a pure market economy, B a command economy, and C is wrong because in a mixed economy resources are owned both privately and by the state. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: profit is the main motivating factor.
the role of the price mechanism is absent.
there is some degree of consumer sovereignty.

questions.enonce_markdown: In a market economy,
questions.corrige_markdown: In a market (free enterprise) economy, resources are mainly privately owned and decisions about what, how and for whom to produce are taken by individual consumers and firms. Prices, which respond to demand and supply, signal scarcity and direct resources to their most profitable uses. This is the price mechanism, so D is correct. State ownership (A), centralised decisions (B) and planning on the basis of needs (C) are features of a command (centrally planned) economy. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: most of the resources are state-owned.
production is planned on the basis of needs.
allocation of resources is determined mostly by the price mechanism.

questions.enonce_markdown: As resources are shifted from the production of one good to the production of another, this can be shown by
questions.corrige_markdown: A production possibilities frontier (PPF) shows the maximum combinations of two goods that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used. Moving resources from one good to the other changes the combination produced but not the total productive capacity, so the economy moves from one point to another **along** the same frontier, and the opportunity cost is the amount of the first good given up. A shift of the frontier (outward or inward) would need a change in the quantity or quality of resources or in technology. Options B and D are in fact identical in meaning and both wrong. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: a movement along the production possibilities frontier.
an outward shift of the production possibilities frontier.
an inward shift of the production possibilities frontier.
an outward shift in the production possibilities frontier.

questions.enonce_markdown: Tertiary production includes
questions.corrige_markdown: Production is classified into three sectors. Primary production extracts natural resources (farming, fishing, mining, oil extraction). Secondary production transforms materials into finished goods (manufacturing, construction). Tertiary production supplies services (banking, insurance, transport, trade, education). Insurance is a service, so A is correct; B and D are primary and C is secondary. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the motives of horizontal integration is to
questions.corrige_markdown: Horizontal integration is the merger of firms at the **same stage** of production in the same industry (for example two cement producers). Its main motives are to gain economies of scale, to eliminate duplication and reorganise (rationalise) production more efficiently, and to reduce competition and increase market power. Safeguarding raw materials (C) is the motive for backward vertical integration, securing market outlets (D) for forward vertical integration, and diversifying output (B) for conglomerate (lateral) integration. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: secure an adequate number of market outlets.

questions.enonce_markdown: When a public company issues new shares by writing to its existing shareholders offering them the chance of buying them in proportion of their existing shareholdings, this is referred to as
questions.corrige_markdown: A rights issue gives existing shareholders the right to buy new shares, usually at a discount, in proportion to the shares they already hold (for example one new share for every four held). A placing sells the shares directly to selected institutional investors, an offer for sale invites the general public to buy shares through an issuing house, and in an issue by tender investors bid for the shares at the price they are ready to pay. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Question 9 refers to the following list of goods: collective goods, merit goods, public producer goods, public goods. From the list above, choose the item which best describes a state University in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: Higher education is the classic example of a **merit good**: the state provides it, charges little or nothing compared with its cost, and subsidises it because consumers under-value its benefits (a more skilled labour force, higher productivity, positive externalities) and would consume too little if left to the market. It is also rival and excludable (places are limited and a fee or entry test applies), so it is not a pure public (collective) good, which is non-rival and non-excludable like street lighting or national defence. 'Public producer goods' are goods and services produced and sold by state-owned enterprises on commercial lines (for example electricity or water), which is not the main character of a state university. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Malthusian theory of population is based on
questions.corrige_markdown: Thomas Malthus argued that population tends to grow in a geometric progression (1, 2, 4, 8, ...) while food production grows only in an arithmetic progression (1, 2, 3, 4, ...). Population would therefore outrun food supply, and the gap would be closed by 'checks' such as famine, disease and war unless 'preventive checks' (late marriage, restraint) were used. The theory is thus based on population growing faster than food production (D). The law of diminishing returns is used to explain why food production slows down, but it is not the basis stated in the options. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the law of diminishing returns to the variable factor.
the fact that population is a source of labour and market for goods and services.
the law of diminishing returns to scale.
the fact that population grows faster than food production.

questions.enonce_markdown: A country with a population of 20 million people experiences 500,000 births and 300,000 deaths in the same year, 1990. Its natural growth rate is
questions.corrige_markdown: The natural growth rate of population is the difference between the birth rate and the death rate, ignoring migration. Natural increase $= 500\,000 - 300\,000 = 200\,000$ people. Natural growth rate $= \dfrac{200\,000}{20\,000\,000} \times 100 = 1\%$. The traps are 25% (births divided by deaths minus one) and 10% or 15% (dividing by the wrong base). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 12 is based on Table 1 below.

**Table 1**

| Loaves of bread | Marginal utility (in utils) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 20 |
| 2 | 15 |
| 3 | 10 |
| 4 | 10 |
| 5 | -5 |

What is the total utility of consuming the 3rd loaf of bread?
questions.corrige_markdown: Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities of all the units consumed up to that unit: $TU_3 = MU_1 + MU_2 + MU_3 = 20 + 15 + 10 = 45$ utils. A (20) is the marginal utility of the first loaf, B (35) is the total utility of two loaves, and the marginal utility of the third loaf is only 10. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 13 is based on Figure 1 below showing a demand curve.

![fig-1](gce-al-economics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

The coefficient of price elasticity of demand at point E is most likely to be
questions.corrige_markdown: The demand curve in Figure 1 is a straight line from $(0, 5)$ on the price axis to $(5, 0)$ on the quantity axis, so $P = 5 - Q$ with $Q$ in thousands. At point E, $P = 1$ and $Q = 4$ (thousand). Along a straight line, a fall of 1 in price raises quantity by 1 (thousand), so $\Delta Q/\Delta P = 1$ in absolute value. Then $PED = \dfrac{\Delta Q}{\Delta P} \times \dfrac{P}{Q} = 1 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$. Demand is inelastic at E, as it is on the lower half of any straight-line demand curve (elasticity is 1 at the midpoint $P = 2.5$). Option B (4) results from inverting the ratio $P/Q$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A Giffen good is one whose
questions.corrige_markdown: A Giffen good is an inferior good which takes up a large part of the budget of poor consumers (for example a staple food like cassava or maize meal). When its price rises, the negative income effect is so strong that it outweighs the substitution effect, so the quantity demanded **rises** and the demand curve slopes upward. A describes a normal good, C is the cross-price effect for complements (a rise in the price of a complement lowers demand), which is not a feature of a Giffen good, and D is wrong because for a Giffen good the two effects work in opposite directions. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: quantity demanded rises with a rise in its price.
demand rises with a rise in the price of a complement.
income and substitution effects work in the same direction.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 15 is based on Figure 2 below.

![fig-2](gce-al-economics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

What is the technical term used in economics to describe the price P1 set by the government below which it becomes illegal to sell?
questions.corrige_markdown: In Figure 2 the price P1 lies above the equilibrium price Pe. A government-set price above equilibrium under which it is illegal to sell is a **minimum price (price floor)**, as with a guaranteed minimum price for coffee or cocoa farmers or a minimum wage. At P1 quantity supplied (Q2) exceeds quantity demanded (Q1), so there is a surplus. A maximum price (ceiling) is set below equilibrium (P2 in the figure) and makes it illegal to sell above it; a black market price is an illegal price which arises when a ceiling creates a shortage. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The supply of a good is represented by the equation, **P = 10 + 0.8Qs**, where P refers to price and Qs is the quantity of the good sold. At what price will the producer sell 20 units?
questions.corrige_markdown: Substitute $Q_s = 20$ into the supply equation: $P = 10 + 0.8 \times 20 = 10 + 16 = 26$. The producer will sell 20 units at a price of 26. Option B (16) is only the term $0.8 Q_s$ and omits the constant 10. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The cost that a firm incurs in purchasing or hiring any factor of production is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Explicit costs are the actual money payments a firm makes to buy or hire factors of production and inputs, such as wages, rent, raw materials and interest. Implicit costs are the opportunity costs of resources the firm already owns (for example the owner's own labour or capital), which involve no payment. Total cost and variable cost are classifications by behaviour with output, not by whether a payment is made to outsiders. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a firm sets its price low enough to discourage new entrants, it can be said to be practicing
questions.corrige_markdown: Limit pricing means that an established firm (often a dominant firm or oligopolist) sets a price low enough to make entry unprofitable for new firms, while still earning at least normal profit. Predatory pricing sets the price below cost in order to drive existing rivals out of the market, cost plus pricing adds a fixed mark-up to average cost, and penetration pricing uses a low launch price to win market share. The wording 'discourage new entrants' points to limit pricing. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 19 is based on Table 2 below showing the weekly output of a firm and its total costs.

**Table 2**

| Output (tonnes) | Total costs (MCFA) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 120 |
| 10 | 180 |
| 20 | 200 |
| 30 | 210 |
| 40 | 225 |

At which level of output is average variable cost lowest?
questions.corrige_markdown: Total cost at zero output is 120, so total fixed cost is 120 MCFA. Total variable cost $= TC - TFC$, and $AVC = TVC/Q$. At 10 tonnes: $(180 - 120)/10 = 6.0$. At 20 tonnes: $(200 - 120)/20 = 4.0$. At 30 tonnes: $(210 - 120)/30 = 3.0$. At 40 tonnes: $(225 - 120)/40 = 2.625$. Average variable cost keeps falling over this range and is lowest at 40 tonnes. Fixed cost must be subtracted: dividing the total cost by output would give average total cost, not average variable cost. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 20 is based on Figure 3, showing the costs and revenue curves for a firm that produces 100 units of a good.

![fig-3](gce-al-economics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

What is the total loss for producing 100 units of output?
questions.corrige_markdown: Read the curves at the output of 100 units. The vertical axis is in thousands of FCFA, so total cost $TC = 250$ (that is 250,000 FCFA), which agrees with $TVC + TFC = 150 + 100 = 250$, and total revenue $TR = 200$ (200,000 FCFA). Loss $= TC - TR = 250\,000 - 200\,000 = 50\,000$ FCFA, so the firm makes a loss since TR is below TC. A (250,000) is the total cost only. B and D come from multiplying the thousand-FCFA readings by the 100 units, although the curves already show **totals**. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of a group of producers who agree to fix common price and output quotas in an oligopolistic market is called a
questions.corrige_markdown: A cartel is a formal agreement among independent producers in an oligopolistic market to fix a common price and/or to share out output quotas, so as to behave like a monopolist and raise joint profit (OPEC is the standard example). A pool is an informal arrangement to share a market or profits and is not defined by quotas on output, a merger is the combination of firms into one, and a conglomerate is a firm with interests in unrelated industries. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 22 is based on Table 3 below showing idle balances at various interest rates. Assume that the demand for active balances stands at 3,000 FCFA. The supply of money is autonomous and stands at 10,000 FCFA.

**Table 3**

| Rate of interest | Speculative demand |
|---|---|
| 8% | 3,000 FCFA |
| 7% | 4,000 FCFA |
| 6% | 6,000 FCFA |
| 5% | 7,000 FCFA |
| 4% | 8,000 FCFA |

The market equilibrium rate of interest is
questions.corrige_markdown: Total demand for money is the demand for active balances (transactions and precautionary) plus the speculative demand for idle balances: $L = 3\,000 + L_s$. The money market is in equilibrium when the fixed supply of 10,000 FCFA equals total demand, so the speculative demand must equal $10\,000 - 3\,000 = 7\,000$ FCFA. Table 3 shows a speculative demand of 7,000 FCFA at an interest rate of 5%. At 6% total demand would be $3\,000 + 6\,000 = 9\,000 < 10\,000$ (excess supply of money, so the rate falls) and at 4% it would be $3\,000 + 8\,000 = 11\,000 > 10\,000$ (excess demand, so the rate rises). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In order to increase the labour force from 10 to 11 persons, a firm is obliged to raise the weekly wage rate per worker from 100,000 FCFA to 104,000 FCFA. The marginal cost is
questions.corrige_markdown: Because the firm must raise the wage for **all** its workers to attract the extra one (it faces an upward-sloping labour supply curve), the marginal cost of labour is the change in the total wage bill. Wage bill with 10 workers $= 10 \times 100\,000 = 1\,000\,000$ FCFA. Wage bill with 11 workers $= 11 \times 104\,000 = 1\,144\,000$ FCFA. Marginal cost $= 1\,144\,000 - 1\,000\,000 = 144\,000$ FCFA. The wage of the eleventh worker alone (104,000, option C) is the average cost, not the marginal cost, and 140,000 or 145,000 come from adding the rise only partly. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When land has only one use, all of its income is economic rent because
questions.corrige_markdown: Economic rent is the part of a factor's earnings above its transfer earnings, that is above what is needed to keep it in its present use (its opportunity cost). If land has only one use, there is no alternative use to which it could be transferred, so its opportunity cost (transfer earnings) is zero and all of its income is economic rent. The supply of such land is perfectly inelastic, not elastic (C), and transfer earnings are zero, not positive (A). Having an alternative use (D) would create transfer earnings. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Normal profit is
questions.corrige_markdown: Normal profit is the minimum reward needed to keep the entrepreneur in the present line of production. It is counted as part of the firm's costs (the opportunity cost of entrepreneurship), so when a firm earns only normal profit its total revenue just covers total costs: $TR - TC = 0$, which means zero economic (abnormal or supernormal) profit. If $TR - TC$ is positive (B) the firm earns abnormal profit above normal profit. Option D confuses profit with average cost and A is a loose description of the rate of return in the industry rather than the condition stated in terms of TR and TC. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the average rate of profit for the industry.
when TR minus TC is positive.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following items should be included in national income accounting?
questions.corrige_markdown: National income measures the value of goods and services newly produced in a period, so only payments for **current production** count. The commission earned by an estate agent is the reward for a current service, so it is included even though the house is old (the sale price of the house is excluded, the commission is not). The sale of second-hand cars (A) is a transfer of an existing asset (only the dealer's margin would count), winnings from games of chance (B) and unemployment benefits (D) are transfer payments for which no good or service is produced. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Commission earned from the sale of a house built 25 years ago.

questions.enonce_markdown: Gross national product exceeds gross domestic product by the amount of
questions.corrige_markdown: $GNP = GDP + \text{net property income from abroad}$, where net property income from abroad is the income earned by nationals on assets they own abroad (profits, interest, dividends) minus the income paid to foreign owners of assets located in the country. When this net figure is positive, GNP exceeds GDP. Transfer payments (A) are excluded from both, capital consumption (B) is the difference between gross and net measures, and property income paid abroad (C) would only reduce GNP relative to GDP. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A measure of national expenditure at market prices does not reflect the true value of factor costs because it includes
questions.corrige_markdown: National expenditure is measured at the prices consumers actually pay. These prices include indirect taxes (VAT, excise duties), which raise the price above what producers receive, and are lowered by subsidies, which reduce the price below the cost of the factors. To obtain the value at factor cost: $\text{GDP at factor cost} = \text{GDP at market prices} - \text{indirect taxes} + \text{subsidies}$. Direct taxes (B) are taxes on income, which do not enter the prices of goods, and transfer payments (C) are not part of expenditure on output. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a 4-sector economy, which of the following conditions holds for national income to be in equilibrium?
questions.corrige_markdown: A four-sector economy has households, firms, government and the foreign sector. National income is in equilibrium when total injections equal total leakages. Injections are investment $I$, government spending $G$ and exports $X$; leakages are saving $S$, taxes $T$ and imports $M$. The condition is therefore $I + G + X = S + T + M$, which is option B written in a different order. Consumption $C$ is neither an injection nor a leakage, so it must not appear (A and D), and C omits the foreign sector (it is the equilibrium condition of a 3-sector economy). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: C + I + X = S + T + M.
X + I + G = S + M + T.
G + I + C = S + T + M.

questions.enonce_markdown: A man has a rise in income from 25,000 to 27,000. As a result, his saving rises from 900 to 1300. His MPC is
questions.corrige_markdown: Change in income $\Delta Y = 27\,000 - 25\,000 = 2\,000$. Change in saving $\Delta S = 1\,300 - 900 = 400$. Therefore $MPS = \Delta S/\Delta Y = 400/2\,000 = 0.2$. Change in consumption $\Delta C = 2\,000 - 400 = 1\,600$, so $MPC = \Delta C/\Delta Y = 1\,600/2\,000 = 0.8$, and $MPC + MPS = 1$. Option A (0.2) is the marginal propensity to save. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The determinants of the multiplier in a closed economy without government are
questions.corrige_markdown: In a closed economy without government there are no imports, exports or taxes. The only leakage is saving, so the multiplier is $k = \dfrac{1}{1 - MPC} = \dfrac{1}{MPS}$, which depends on the marginal propensity to consume and the marginal propensity to save (which are complementary, $MPC + MPS = 1$). Imports and taxes (A, B) are leakages only in an open economy or in an economy with a government, and exports (C) are an injection, not a determinant of the multiplier. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In an economy where investment is autonomous, an attempt to increase saving will lead to
questions.corrige_markdown: This is the **paradox of thrift**. In equilibrium, planned saving equals planned investment. If investment is autonomous (fixed, independent of income), $I$ does not change when households try to save more. The extra saving reduces consumption and so aggregate demand and income through the multiplier. Income keeps falling until saving falls back to the unchanged level of investment. Total saving at the new equilibrium is therefore the same as before (equal to $I$), although income is lower. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: an initial rise and subsequent decrease in total saving.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 33 refers to a change in the rate of spending on exports which causes a change in income as follows: 100 + 90 + 81 + 72.9 + X + ...

What is the value of X?
questions.corrige_markdown: Each term is 0.9 times the previous one: $90 = 100 \times 0.9$, $81 = 90 \times 0.9$, $72.9 = 81 \times 0.9$. This is the successive rounds of spending of the multiplier process with a marginal propensity to consume (spent in each round) of 0.9. So $X = 72.9 \times 0.9 = 65.61$. Option A (59.05) is the term after X ($65.61 \times 0.9 = 59.049$), B (153.9) is the sum of the two previous terms ($81 + 72.9$) and D (190) is the sum of the first two terms ($100 + 90$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the Accounting or Average Rate of Return (ARR) method of investment appraisal?
questions.corrige_markdown: The ARR is the average annual profit from a project divided by the (average or initial) capital invested. It is easy to calculate (so A is wrong) and needs no discount rate or trial and error (B and C describe the Net Present Value and the Internal Rate of Return methods). Its main weakness is that it treats profits earned in different years as equal and **ignores the time value of money**: a franc received in year 5 is worth less than a franc received in year 1. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Dependence on trial and error for its estimation.
Relies on the choice of a discount rate.
Ignores the time value of money.

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of money will fall when the
questions.corrige_markdown: The value (purchasing power) of money is the inverse of the general price level. It falls when prices rise, that is when the rate of inflation is positive, because each franc buys fewer goods. A falling price level (A) and deflation (D) raise the value of money. If the growth of the money supply falls below the growth of output (C), the price level tends to fall, so the value of money tends to rise. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: growth of money supply falls below the growth of output.
economy experiences a period of deflation.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 36 is based on the following data on table 4 below.

**Table 4**

| Commodity | Expenditure 2005 (FCFA) | Price index 2005 | Price index 2007 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drinks | 200 | 100 | 150 |
| Housing | 300 | 100 | 80 |
| Food | 500 | 100 | 120 |

The weighted price index shows that between 2005 and 2007, the general price level rose by
questions.corrige_markdown: The weights are the shares of expenditure in the base year: drinks $200/1\,000 = 0.2$, housing $300/1\,000 = 0.3$ and food $500/1\,000 = 0.5$. Weighted index for 2007 $= 0.2 \times 150 + 0.3 \times 80 + 0.5 \times 120 = 30 + 24 + 60 = 114$. The base-year index is 100, so the general price level rose by $114 - 100 = 14\%$. A (50%) is the rise of the drinks index alone, B (16.66%) comes from the simple unweighted average $(150 + 80 + 120)/3 = 116.67$, which ignores the weights, and D (5%) does not match any valid calculation. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following assets of a commercial bank represents the bank's lending to the government?
questions.corrige_markdown: A commercial bank lends to the government by buying Treasury bills (short-term government securities, which are liquid and carry no default risk) and government bonds. Advances (A) are loans and overdrafts to private customers, money at call and short notice (C) is lent to other financial institutions such as discount houses, and balances at the central bank (D) are the bank's reserves. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Money at call and short notice.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given a bank's cash ratio of 10%, what will be the maximum deposits it can create from an initial deposit of 150 million FCFA?
questions.corrige_markdown: The credit multiplier is the reciprocal of the cash ratio: $k = \dfrac{1}{0.10} = 10$. The maximum total deposits are $10 \times 150 = 1\,500$ million FCFA, which includes the initial deposit of 150 million. The additional deposits created by lending are therefore 1,350 million FCFA (option A), which is the amount of credit created, not the total deposits. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A regressive tax can best be described as one whose marginal tax rate is
questions.corrige_markdown: A regressive tax takes a **smaller percentage** of income as income rises, so the average tax rate falls with income. The average rate can only fall if each extra franc of income is taxed at a rate lower than the average, that is if the marginal tax rate is less than the average tax rate. A proportional tax has equal marginal and average rates (A), and a progressive tax has a marginal rate greater than the average rate (C). D is true of both progressive and regressive taxes, so it does not describe a regressive tax specifically. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: equal to the average tax rate.
less than the average tax rate.
greater than the average tax rate.
not equal to the average tax rate.

questions.enonce_markdown: The point at which the tax burden finally settles is described as tax
questions.corrige_markdown: The **incidence** of a tax is the final resting place of the burden, that is who actually bears the tax after it has been shifted through changes in prices, wages or profits (for example, a tax on producers may be passed on to consumers as a higher price). The tax base is what is taxed (income, goods, property), 'burden' is the cost carried by the taxpayer, and a 'heaven' (tax haven) is a country with very low taxes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a government contracts loans at lower interest rates which were contracted at very high interest rates, it is described as
questions.corrige_markdown: Refinancing means raising new loans, usually on better terms such as lower interest rates, in order to repay old debts contracted on worse terms. Funding is the conversion of short-term debt (floating debt) into long-term debt, rescheduling is a renegotiation of repayment dates with creditors, and floating debt is short-term government borrowing such as Treasury bills. The question describes borrowing at a lower rate to pay off high-rate loans. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The deliberate manipulation of government income and expenditure to achieve macro-economic objectives is known as
questions.corrige_markdown: Fiscal policy is the deliberate use of government income (taxation) and expenditure to influence the level of economic activity and to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as growth, full employment and price stability. This is the standard definition and the answer expected here. Automatic stabilizers (D, and 'automatic fiscal policy' C) work without any deliberate decision (for example progressive taxes and unemployment benefits), so they do not fit the word 'deliberate'. Discretionary fiscal policy (B) is a subset of fiscal policy involving deliberate changes in tax rates or spending, but the question defines the general concept. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 43 is based on Figure 4 below showing the demand and supply of wheat in an economy before and after a tariff imposition.

![fig-4](gce-al-economics-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

What was the quantity of wheat imported before the tariff imposition?
questions.corrige_markdown: Before the tariff the country buys at the world price of 100 (000 FCFA per tonne). At that price domestic supply is 100 tonnes (where the supply curve S meets the price line) and domestic demand is 500 tonnes (where the demand curve D meets the price line). Imports are the excess of demand over domestic supply: $500 - 100 = 400$ tonnes. After the tariff the price rises to 140; supply is then 200 tonnes and demand 400 tonnes, so imports fall to $400 - 200 = 200$ tonnes. Option B (300) is the equilibrium quantity without trade, and D (100) is the domestic supply only. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main argument for protecting domestic industries is to
questions.corrige_markdown: The classic argument for protection is the **infant industry argument**: a new domestic industry starts with small output and high unit costs and cannot yet compete with established foreign firms. Temporary tariffs or quotas give it time to grow, to reach a large scale and to benefit from economies of scale, after which it can compete without protection. Protection does not encourage dumping (C), which is selling abroad below cost and is a reason for **anti-dumping** duties. Preventing unemployment (B) and helping declining industries to restructure (D) are also arguments sometimes used, but they are secondary to the infant industry case. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: enable them to develop economies of scale.
prevent a rapid increase in unemployment.
enable them restructure and be more competitive.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 45 is based on Table 5 below.

**Table 5**

| Country | Computers (millions) | Oil (millions of barrels) |
|---|---|---|
| X | 10 | 100 |
| Y | 1 | 80 |

Which of the following statements is true? Country X has
questions.corrige_markdown: Compute the opportunity cost of each good in each country. Country X: 1 computer costs $100/10 = 10$ barrels of oil, and 1 barrel of oil costs $10/100 = 0.1$ computer. Country Y: 1 computer costs $80/1 = 80$ barrels of oil, and 1 barrel of oil costs $1/80 = 0.0125$ computer. X gives up fewer barrels per computer (10 against 80), so X has a **lesser opportunity cost in computers** and a comparative advantage in computers (A is true). C is false: X's opportunity cost of oil (0.1 computer) is higher than Y's (0.0125). B and D speak of 'cost' and not of opportunity cost: X produces more of both goods than Y (10 against 1 computers and 100 against 80 barrels of oil), which means X has an absolute advantage in both goods, so its real cost is lower and not greater in both. (B is true only in the sense of opportunity cost, which it does not say.) **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: lesser opportunity cost in the production of computers.
greater cost in the production of oil.
lesser opportunity cost in the production of oil.
greater cost in the production of computers.

questions.enonce_markdown: The balance of payments deficit for a country will reduce, other things being equal if;
questions.corrige_markdown: A deficit means that imports and other payments exceed exports and other receipts. If the country's prices fall relative to foreign prices, its exports become cheaper to foreigners and imports become dearer to residents, so export earnings rise and import spending falls, which reduces the deficit. A rise in domestic income relative to foreign income (A) raises imports. A fall in the domestic price of the foreign currency (C) is an appreciation of the home currency, which makes exports dearer and imports cheaper, worsening the deficit. Lowering tariffs (D) makes imports cheaper and increases them. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: its level of GNP rises relative to foreign GNP.
its prices fall relative to foreign prices.
the domestic price of the foreign currency falls.

questions.enonce_markdown: A sustained increase in the real GDP is described as
questions.corrige_markdown: Economic growth is defined as a sustained (long-term) increase in real GDP, or in real GDP per head. 'Real' means the effect of price changes has been removed. Actual growth (A) is the year-to-year increase in the output actually produced and does not need to be sustained, potential growth (B) is the increase in productive capacity, and economic development (D) is a wider concept involving improvements in living standards, health, education and the structure of the economy. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
To promote growth, countries should

*Options as printed:* A) change the level of technology.   B) promote ssavings.   C) promote investment .   D) discourage human capital investment.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth rises when the productive capacity of the economy rises. The most direct policy is to **promote investment** in physical capital (machines, factories, infrastructure) and in human capital, because investment raises the capital stock and productivity. Discouraging human capital investment (D) would reduce growth. Promoting savings (B) helps only if the savings are channelled into investment, and 'change the level of technology' (A) does not say in which direction, so C is the best answer.

**Intended answer: C (promote investment ).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Philip's curve seems to indicate that the government is faced with a choice between which two of the following objectives?

i) Inflation.

ii) Full employment.

iii) A balance of payments surplus.

iv) A high rate of growth.

*Options as printed:* A) (i) and (ii).   B) (i) and (iii).   C) (ii) and(iii).   D) (i) and (ii).
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Phillips curve shows an inverse relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment: when the government reduces unemployment towards full employment, demand pressure raises wages and prices, and when it lowers inflation, unemployment tends to rise. The trade-off is therefore between (i) low inflation and (ii) full employment. The balance of payments and the growth rate are not the variables of the Phillips curve. Options A and D are printed identically as '(i) and (ii)'.

**Intended answer: A ((i) and (ii)).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A more equitable distribution of income will reduce

*Options as printed:* A) the standard of living.   B) inflation.   C) consumption.   D) unemployment.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A more equitable distribution transfers purchasing power from high-income households, which save a larger share of extra income, to low-income households, which have a higher marginal propensity to consume. Total consumption therefore rises (so C is wrong) and so does aggregate demand, which stimulates output and employment, so **unemployment** tends to fall. A fairer distribution also tends to raise the standard of living of the poor (A is wrong), and it does not by itself reduce inflation (B), since extra demand puts, if anything, upward pressure on prices. D is the only option that can be defended as reduced.

**Intended answer: D (unemployment).**
